text:
anya: Quick update — during magnet32k-int4 bring-up I ran a long-prefill sweep (12k tokens) and saw a reproducible 'rising tail' where early-history attention weight patterns fade then reassert near token ~8192. Not typical drift — looks like a RoPE hinge/rescale at a window boundary combined with KV index shift. Repro script and minimal prompt below.

sara: ugh. did you see logits or just final output drift? any quant vs fp32 difference?

anya: both. At int4 the per-token logit gaps to fp32 grow steadily between 7.5–8.3k, then many logits snap back, producing hallucinated repeats. In fp32 the gap is stable.

mike: can you paste the minimal repro snippet + the exact model/quant flags? might be a prefilling alignment problem.

anya: sure — run something like:

```bash
python tests/long_prefill_probe.py \--model magnet32k_int4_v1 \--prefill 12000 \--seed 42 \--kv-shard 256 \--rope-scaling=legacy
```

The important bits: shard=256, sequence not multiple of 256, rope-scaling mode set to legacy quant path. In canary I toggled rope-scaling=stable and issue disappears.

oliver: interesting. that suggests two potential causes: 1) RoPE phase multiply uses different interpolation in the quant kernel, 2) KV index calculation wraps incorrectly when prefill length % shard != 0.

anya: yep. I instrumented kv indices and saw occasional -1 effective index for a tiny fraction of heads at the hinge moment, which then triggers an out-of-order read that later gets masked but perturbs attention normalization.

prefill-bot: automated check ran: compare_attention_indices produced mismatch_count=12 for run 1749992021, head_ids=[3,7,11], positions ~8190..8202. Link: https://internal.ci/runs/1749992021/indices

mike: low-effort triage plan: (a) reproduce with shard=512 and shard=128 to see scaling; (b) run same script with quantized kernel replaced by fp32 for just the RoPE multiply; (c) add guard to kv index math to avoid negative indices.

anya: I ran (a): shard=512 less/no issue, shard=128 worse (more frequent snaps). (b) swapping to fp32-rope removed the snap. (c) simple guard reduces symptom but not root cause.

sara: ok sounds like quant kernel interpolation + off-by-chunk arithmetic. Can we bisect kernel changes? which commit introduced the quant RoPE rewrite?

oliver: commit f3b2a7c — refactor/quant-rope-optim — landed 3 weeks ago. I'll bisect locally. If it's that, rollback or add runtime fallback to fp32-rope for long-prefill until we have a fix.

anya: adding an internal eval: long-prefill-quality (generate 10 prompts, measure KL over moving windows and token-repetition rate). Current int4 baseline shows KL spike at hinge ~8192, fp32 baseline doesn't. I pushed metrics to the onboarding dashboard: https://console/redwood/evals/long-prefill/1749992021

mike: let's also add a canary rule: if prefill > 8000 and model.quant == int4 then route RoPE to fp32 path, as a temporary mitigation. Add a perf note — we expect ~6–8% token latency increase for affected calls.

anya: will open a PR for the guard + canary routing and include testcases. Assigning to oliver for the kernel bisect (he can revert if needed).

oliver: ack. I'll run git bisect against f3b2a7c..HEAD and report which diff introduces index arithmetic change.

anya: thanks — tagging @sara for rollout decision after bisect. :thumbsup:

sara: thanks all. if anyone sees similar behavior on other models (atlas28k / boreas32k), drop a message here.

mike: ping me if you want me to wire the canary rule into routing policies — quick to add.

anya: filing the thread summary in the onboarding doc once we have bisect result.
